q: 1. The unit of payment for road side brick edging to increase the pavement width is
explain: as per key c .Edging or borders along roads are measured in running meters.

q: 2. The unit of payment for excavation trenches for pipes, cables etc. upto 1.5 m depth in ordinary rock/hard rock is
explain: Narrow trenches for utility lines are often measured by running length (r m) for a specified depth range.

q: 3. No deductions is made in the masonry for the openings if the area of the opening does not exceed
explain: Small openings up to 0.10 m2 in area are considered negligible and no deduction is made for them while measuring masonry quantity.

q: 4. *The quantity of jafri is measured in terms of
explain: Jafri (lattice work) is measured by area in square meters.

q: 5. The density of cement is generally taken as
explain: For estimating purposes, the loose bulk density of ordinary Portland cement is generally taken as approximately 1500 kg/m3.

q: 6. *Form work is measured in
explain: Formwork (shuttering) for concrete is measured by the area of the surface in contact with the concrete.

q: 7. The depth of shallow manhole is taken as
explain: A shallow manhole is generally taken to have a depth of about 2 m, used for lighter/lower-depth sewer lines.

q: 8. The number of corrugations in a GCI sheet is
explain: A standard galvanised corrugated iron (GCI) sheet of standard width contains 10 corrugations.

q: 9. The expected out turn of brick work in cement mortar in foundation and plinth per mason per day, is
explain: Brick masonry laid in foundation and plinth (simpler, less finishing work than superstructure) has a higher expected daily output of about 1.75 m³ per mason.

q: 10. *The unit of door frame chaukhat is
explain: The wooden frame (chaukhat) is measured by its volume in cubic meters.

q: 11. The unit of measurement of supply of pipe (diameter and type specified) is
explain: Once the diameter and type of pipe are specified, its supply quantity is conventionally taken by weight (kg), since pipe cost is largely material-weight based.

q: 12. The area of the segmental portion of an arch with span l and riser r is approximately given by
explain: The area of a segmental (parabolic-like) arch portion with span l and rise r is approximated by the standard formula (2/3) × l × r, derived from parabolic segment area.

q: 13. Normally the ratio of span to effective depth of a beam is
explain: For preliminary sizing of RCC beams, a span-to-effective-depth ratio of about 10 to 12 is normally adopted for typical simply supported beams.

q: 14. In long and short wall method of estimation, the length of long wall is the center to center space between walls plus
options: half of the breadth of wall on each side
one forth of the breadth of wall on each side
explain: The formula for the length of a long wall is (C/C length + 2 x half width), which equals C/C length + one full breadth.

q: 15. The weight of 10 mm diameter mild steel rod per meter length is equal to
explain: Using the standard formula (d^2/162) kg/m for mild steel bars, a 10 mm bar weighs approximately 0.617 kg/m, rounded to 0.62 kg.

q: 16. The volume of cement required for 10 m³ of brickwork in 1 : 6 cement mortar is approximately equal to
explain: For 1:6 cement mortar used in 10 m³ of brickwork (mortar volume about 3 m³ after deducting brick volume), the cement fraction works out to approximately 3/7 m³ using the standard rate-analysis method.

q: 17. The actual weight of cement bag is more in case of
explain: Paper bags prevent the 'seepage' or loss of fine cement particles better than woven bags, maintaining weight better.

q: 18. The correct prismoidal formula for volume is
options: D (first area + last area + Sum even area + 2*Sum odd areas)
D/3 (first area + last area + 4*Sum even area + 2*Sum odd areas)
D/3 (first area + last area + 2*Sum even area + 4 odd areas)
D/6 (first area + last area + 2*Sum even area + 4*Sum odd areas)
explain: The prismoidal formula for volume is V = D/3 [first area + last area + 4(sum of even-numbered section areas) + 2(sum of odd-numbered section areas)], analogous to Simpson's rule.

q: 19. The area of a sloping surface of a protective embankment of mean height d, side slopes S:1 and length L is
explain: The sloping surface area of an embankment side is the slope length (d*sqrt(1+s^2)) multiplied by the embankment length L, giving L.d.sqrt(1+s^2).

q: 20. The volume of cement required for 10 m^3 of brick work in 1:6 cement mortar is approximately equal to
explain: 10 m^3 brickwork requires ~3 m^3 mortar. Cement = 3 / (1+6) = 3/7 m^3.

q: 21. The number of handmade brick required for 1 m³ of brick work is
explain: Since handmade (non-modular) bricks are slightly larger/irregular compared to standard modular bricks, about 530 handmade bricks are required per cubic metre of brickwork.

q: 22. While estimating for lintel over openings, if the dimension for bearing is not given, the bearing is usually taken as equal to
options: half the thickness of lintel or 12 cm whichever is higher
thickness of lintel with a minimum of 12 cm
twice the thickness of lintel with a minimum of 12 cm
explain: When not specified, the standard bearing length for a lintel over an opening is taken equal to the lintel's own thickness, subject to a minimum of 12 cm.

q: 23. The unit of measurement of fair face brick work is
explain: Fair-face brickwork refers to the finished exposed brick surface treatment, so it is measured as a surface-finishing item in square metres.

q: 24. The quantity of thermoplastic paint for 300 m2 on smooth road surface (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: The requirement for 300m2 is listed as 1200 liters in the provided key.

q: 25. *The nominal lead and lift allowed for the earthwork in the excavations of the foundations are (NS norm)
explain: Nepal Standards (NS) align with the general 30m horizontal lead and 1.5m vertical lift for basic excavation rates.

q: 26. In case of steel rolling shutter, for the estimation of painted area, the plain area is multiplied by
explain: For rolling shutters, the area is calculated as the size of the opening multiplied by 1.10 to 1.25 (1 1/4) to account for corrugations and overlaps, depending on the specific code used.

q: 27. The approximate weight of one cubic meter of mild steel is
explain: The standard density of mild steel used in engineering calculations is 7850 kg/m³.

q: 28. If the bearing is not specified for the lintel, in the estimation it is usually taken as
options: thickness of lintel subjected to a minimum value of 12 cm
3/4 of lintel thickness or 12 cm whichever is larger
explain: If bearing is not specified, the lintel's bearing is conventionally taken equal to the thickness of the lintel itself, subject to a minimum value of 12 cm.

q: 29. In the estimation of plastering surface the deductions are not made for
explain: In plastering estimation, no deductions are made for minor items like ends of beams, ends of rafters, or small openings up to 0.5 m², since the extra plaster elsewhere compensates.

q: 30. The unit of measurement of holdfast is
explain: A hold fast is a small metal fitting whose quantity is measured and paid for by weight, in kg.

q: 31. One hectare-meter represent a volume of
explain: One hectare-meter is the volume obtained by covering one hectare (10,000 m2) with a depth of 1 meter, giving 10,000 m3.

q: 32. The depth of shallow manhole should be more than
explain: A manhole is classified as shallow when its depth exceeds 2.1 m (but remains within a defined lower range) as per standard drainage classification.

q: 33. The volume of sand a normal truck can carry per trip is approximately
explain: A standard-sized truck can typically carry approximately 15 to 20 cubic metres of sand per trip.

q: 34. A document showing the list of quantity of various items of works required for completion of any project is known as
explain: The Schedule of Quantities (or Bill of Quantities) lists the calculated amounts of each work item required.

q: 35. The area of the cross-section of a road fully in banking shown in figure is
explain: For a road fully in embankment on a cross-sloping ground (ground slope r:1, side slope s:1, half formation width b, height d), the standard derived cross-sectional area formula is [sb² + r²(2bd + Sd)²] / (r² - S²), matching option (a).

q: 36. Pick up the excavation where measurements are made in square metres for payment
options: surface dressing up to 15 cm depths
surface excavating up to 30 cm depths
explain: Both surface dressing (up to 15 cm depth) and surface excavation (up to 30 cm depth) are shallow operations paid on an area basis, since their limited, near-uniform depth makes area a more practical measure than volume.

q: 37. The area of one hectare is equal to
explain: One hectare equals a 100 m x 100 m square, which is 10,000 m2.

q: 38. The unit of measurement of brick work in foundation is
explain: Brick work in foundations, being a thick, bulky masonry item, is measured by volume, in cubic metres.

q: 39. In absence of detailed design the percentage of steel in concrete columns is usually taken as
explain: Without detailed structural design, the reinforcement in concrete columns is conventionally assumed at 1 to 5 percent of the gross column area/volume, consistent with code minimum/maximum limits.

q: 40. The approximate percentage by volume of reinforcement for chajja and sunshade is:
explain: Thin RCC members like chajjas and sunshades typically require roughly 0.5% to 0.8% reinforcement.

q: 41. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: pointing is measured in sq. m
plastering is measured in sq. m
striking is measured in sq. m
explain: Pointing, plastering, and striking (formwork removal) are all thin surface-finishing operations, and each is correctly measured by area, in square metres, making all three statements true.

q: 42. The amount provisioned for tools and plants on earthwork excavation item in norms for rate analysis is:
explain: Tools and plants (T&P) charges are often estimated as a percentage of the labor cost for manual excavation.

q: 43. The quantity of stone required to produce 10 m³ of rubble stone masonry will be
explain: Because rubble stone masonry contains voids filled with mortar, more raw stone volume than the finished masonry volume is required; standard rate analysis gives approximately 12.5 m³ of stone for 10 m³ of finished masonry (a factor of about 1.25).

q: 44. Brick walls are measured in sq. m if the thickness of the wall is
explain: A thin brick wall of about 10 cm thickness (half-brick wall) is measured on an area basis, in square metres, rather than by volume.

q: 45. Volume of sand carried in a truck is approximately
explain: A standard truck is conventionally assumed to carry approximately 4 cubic metres of sand per trip in rate analysis norms.

q: 46. One cubic metre of cement concrete (1 : 2 : 4) is to be mixed by volume. Number of cement bags required will be approximately
explain: For 1 m³ of 1:2:4 concrete, dry volume ≈ 1.54 m³, cement fraction = 1/7, giving cement volume ≈ 0.22 m³; dividing by 0.035 m³ per bag gives approximately 6 bags.

q: 47. One cubic metre of mild steel weights about
explain: As established earlier, the density of mild steel is approximately 7850 kg/m³, giving this same weight for one cubic metre.
